newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: U.N. agency to repatriate 10,000 Somali refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency to repatriate 10,000 Somali refugees.

text.p: Ten thousand Somali refugees in Ethiopia will start returning to their home country this month under a voluntary U.N. repatriation programme, a U.N. refugee agency official said on Friday.
Mahary Maasho, spokesman at the Addis Ababa UNHCR office, said the Somalis would be transported to Awdal and Galbeed regions in northwest Somalia.

The 10,000 Somalis are among 280,000 refugees in Ethiopia and come from the Teferiber, Darwanaji and Hartisheik camps close to the border with the self-declared Somaliland Republic and had lived in the camps since the fall of Somali President Siad Barre in 1991.
Some 30,000 people were killed in the clan-based violence that erupted after Barre's fall and around 300,000 more died in an ensuing famine. Hundreds of thousands fled into exile.
The U.N. spokesman said the repatriation was part of a UNHCR programme to send home some 46,000 Somali refugees, including 1,000 from Djibouti and 35,000 from Kenya before the end of the year.
